- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment peaks within 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5 days if sentiment > 0.3.
- Model shows persistent lag in price direction: if true price rises > 1.5% from 3-day average, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% to match momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (e.g., +0.4 → -0.3 → +0.4), model tends to overfit short-term noise; apply smoothing filter or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true price exceeds forecast by > 2% in 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (±0.1) for 3+ days, model tends to drift; apply mean reversion correction: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true recent average.
